p: Shuffleboard looks easy until you try it. The trick is a smooth, controlled push rather than a big shove: keep your arm relaxed, follow through in a straight line and let the puck glide. Too much power and it sails straight off the end; too little and it stops short and becomes a handy blocker for your opponent. Watching how the table plays for the first few goes will pay off later in the game.

For groups, it's worth planning your table time around food and drinks so nobody's juggling a plate and a puck at the same time. Split into teams early, mix up the experienced players and first-timers, and agree whether you're playing for pride or for who buys the next round. If you're organising a work do, sort the booking well in advance, as Docklands venues get busy with office parties, especially in the run-up to Christmas. Age policies can vary at venues like this, so check before bringing anyone under 18.

Make a bit more of your trip to Canary Wharf with a look round the estate. The Crossrail Place Roof Garden, on top of the Elizabeth line station, is a calm, leafy space with plants from around the world, and it's free to wander. The estate also has a programme of public art dotted around its squares and waterside paths. If you'd like a different view, the Thames Clipper river boats stop at Canary Wharf pier, giving you a scenic ride towards Greenwich or central London.
